mil5.1.8:0.4: 8. Question on Cutting Off Unwholesome States
mil5.1.8:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, did the Tathāgata attain omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states, or did he attain omniscience while some unwholesome states remained?”
mil5.1.8:1.2: “Your majesty, the Blessed One attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states. No unwholesome state remained in the Blessed One.”
mil5.1.8:2.1: “But, venerable sir, did painful feeling ever arise in the Tathāgata’s body?”
mil5.1.8:2.2: “Yes, your majesty. At Rājagaha the Blessed One’s foot was pierced by a splinter, and an illness involving bloody discharge (dysentery) arose. When his body was congested, Jīvaka administered a purgative. When a wind ailment arose, the elder who was his attendant (Ānanda) sought out hot water.”
mil5.1.8:3.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, if the Tathāgata attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states, then the statement that the Blessed One’s foot was pierced by a splinter and that he suffered an illness with bloody discharge is false.
mil5.1.8:3.2: But if the Tathāgata’s foot were pierced by a splinter and he suffered an illness with bloody discharge, then the statement that the Tathāgata attained omniscience after burning up all unwholesome states is also false.
mil5.1.8:3.3: Venerable sir, there is no experiencing of feeling without kamma; all feeling is rooted in kamma, and one feels it by way of kamma alone. This double-horned dilemma has now come to you, and it must be resolved by you.”
mil5.1.8:4.1: “Certainly not, your majesty; not all feeling is rooted in kamma.
mil5.1.8:4.2: Feelings arise from eight causes, and by these causes many beings experience feeling.
